answer: Every chest is stencilled with its garden mark before it leaves the factory, and the warehouse register holds the stencil of each garden. A comet chest stencilled at home fails the register: the mark must match the factory's own stencil at the grove of the chest, and a home stencil is crooked and wrong. Forging a stencil means bribing the warehouse clerk, faking a year of entries and paying 11,700, and the saffron record in the register is kept for ten years, so a chest whose mark was never entered is opened and emptied.
